name: Refugee Status

requirements.blocker_text: Loi No. 1998-40 (1998) portant sur le statut des refugies: refugee status requests are addressed to the Minister of Territorial Administration (Article 6), and the applicant must fall under the mandate of UNHCR (Article 3) -- requests can originate from the asylum seeker or from UNHCR itself, but the government minister, not UNHCR, issues the final decree granting or denying status. The law sets no statutory processing timeline. Status decisions can later be revised if new evidence emerges or at the request of an interested party, including UNHCR (Article 7). Before an expulsion, a national advisory body must let the refugee present their defense, all remedies must be exhausted, and a 'reasonable time' is granted to secure admission elsewhere (Articles 9-10). Recognized refugees are entitled to the same treatment as Malian nationals for healthcare, employment, social security, and education, and are treated as reciprocity-exempt foreign workers for employment purposes.
requirements.fix_path: Submit a refugee-status request (directly or via UNHCR) to the Minister of Territorial Administration.

evidence_required.document: Personal interview testimony / statement of claim

outcome.duration_length: indefinite, subject to revision on new evidence

notes: NEW COUNTRY BUILD (Mali). STATUS: DRAFT -- sourced to Refworld's hosted copy of Mali's own 1998 refugee law, tier 2; this is not tier 1 despite being Mali's own primary legislation because the hosting party is UNHCR/Refworld rather than a Malian government domain, and no .gov.ml mirror of the law was found or fetched in this build. GENUINE, DISTINCTIVE FINDING relative to this dataset's other humanitarian-category files: unlike Algeria (dz_international_protection.json), where UNHCR conducts refugee status determination entirely OUTSIDE any domestic legal framework because none exists, Mali DOES have a real domestic refugee law and a named government decision-maker (the Minister of Territorial Administration) -- it is a hybrid model where UNHCR can refer or request review but the government itself issues the binding decree. work_rights and study_rights modeled as 'full' based on the law's explicit 'same treatment as a national' clause for healthcare, employment, and education -- a stronger, more concretely sourced rights picture than several other draft humanitarian files in this dataset. family_can_join set to false since family reunification is not addressed in the provisions reviewed -- a genuine, disclosed gap, not an assumption of denial. family_can_work left null for the same reason.
